original_title: Xbox Says Its Share of GTA 6 Preorders Matches Its Share of the Console Market, Following PS5 Dominance Claim
summary_en: Following reports of PlayStation 5's significant lead in GTA 6 preorders, Xbox has clarified its position, stating that preorder numbers align with its current share of the console market. This statement comes amidst ongoing discussions about platform performance and upcoming sales expectations for the highly anticipated title.
ai_analysis: This situation highlights the complex interplay between platform sales, publisher partnerships, and consumer anticipation in the lead-up to a monumental game release like GTA 6.

en.title: Xbox Responds to GTA 6 PS5 Dominance Claims: Preorders Match Market Share
en.summary: Following reports of PlayStation 5's significant lead in GTA 6 preorders, Xbox has clarified its position, stating that preorder numbers align with its current share of the console market. This statement comes amidst ongoing discussions about platform performance and upcoming sales expectations for the highly anticipated title.
en.body:
Reports suggesting that **Grand Theft Auto VI** preorders are heavily skewed towards the PlayStation 5 have prompted a response from Xbox. While the initial claims, amplified by industry observers, pointed towards a concerning trend for Microsoft's consoles, Xbox CSO **Matthew Ball** has stepped in to offer a different perspective.

Ball insists that Xbox is "very happy" with the current preorder figures for **GTA VI**, noting that the title is already breaking records for the platform. According to internal analysis, Xbox's share of the preorders directly mirrors its current share of the overall console market. This suggests that while the PS5 might be outselling the Xbox Series X/S, the preorder distribution for **GTA VI** on Xbox platforms is performing as expected relative to its install base.

> "Tom, we are very happy with GTA VI pre-orders. The title is breaking records for XBOX, we expect even more records will be broken throughout the fall, and our internal analysis shows our share of preorders to be matching our share of the console market." — Matthew Ball

This clarification arrives at a time when concrete sales figures for the Xbox Series X and S have not been publicly disclosed by Microsoft for several years. In contrast, Sony has announced that the PlayStation 5 has surpassed 95 million units sold as of June 30. Industry analysts have estimated that the combined sales of the Xbox Series range are at least half that of the PS5, indicating a potential 2:1 ratio in favor of Sony's console. If this ratio holds true for **GTA VI** preorders, it would explain the perception of PS5 dominance.

## The Power of Platform Exclusivity and Marketing

Sony's strong partnership with **Rockstar Games** for **GTA VI** is undeniably a significant factor. Sony has strategically leveraged the game in its marketing efforts, prominently featuring the PS5 version in trailers and promotional materials. Furthermore, the console has even received a custom **GTA VI** UI, underscoring the close collaboration. Sony has also been vocal about how specific PS5 features, such as the **DualSense** controller's haptic feedback and adaptive triggers, will enhance the **GTA VI** experience, a detail that likely appeals to fans eager for the most immersive gameplay.

This proactive approach from Sony, coupled with the inherent appeal of **Grand Theft Auto VI** as a system-seller, creates a powerful synergy. The game is widely expected to not only break sales records but also drive a surge in console sales, making the platform battle for **GTA VI** a crucial one for both Microsoft and Sony.

## Looking Ahead to Release

With **Grand Theft Auto VI** slated for release in 2026, the preorder window remains open, and further marketing pushes from both **Rockstar Games** and platform holders are anticipated. Xbox's assertion that preorder performance aligns with market share suggests a confidence in their strategy and player base, even as Sony continues to highlight the unique advantages of the PS5 for this highly anticipated title. Fans on all platforms will be watching closely as more details emerge about the game and its eventual launch.

content_raw: Microsoft has stepped in to address a report that claimed GTA 6 preorders are “heavily skewed” toward PlayStation 5 over Xbox Series X and S. In a report about this week’s layoffs and studios reorganization at Xbox , The Verge’s Tom Warren said the PS5’s dominance over GTA 6 preorders was “ringing yet more alarm bells" about Xbox as a platform. However, Xbox CSO Matthew Ball insisted that Microsoft was “very happy” with GTA 6 preorders, and that its internal data showed preorders were matching “our share of the console market.” Here’s Ball’s statement in full: “Tom, we are very happy with GTA VI pre-orders. The title is breaking records for XBOX, we expect even more records will be broken throughout the fall, and our internal analysis shows our share of preorders to be matching our share of the console market.” While Sony does announce PS5 sales, Microsoft hasn’t announced a number for Xbox Series X and S sales in years. As of June 30, PS5 had sold more than 95 million units. Analysts have suggested the combined Xbox Series range is being outsold by the PS5 by at least a factor of 2:1. If that ratio holds true, there are likely twice as many GTA 6 preorders for PS5 than for Xbox Series X and S. Sony and Rockstar Games' partnership for GTA 6 wil be having a big impact on preorders, too. Sony has leaned heavily into GTA 6, which you can understand given we’re talking about a video game that is expected to break sales records and spark a surge in console sales. This has led to GTA 6 gameplay focusing on the PS5 version, the PS5 showing up in marketing materials for GTA 6, and even a custom GTA 6 UI for Sony’s console . Sony has published blog posts talking about the features of the PS5 that GTA 6 will use, such as the speaker in the DualSense controller and the pad's haptic feedback. Other additions to GTA 6's PS5 marketing campaign include a version of the PlayStation app logo on smartphones that features GTA 6 colors and pale tree fronds. So, with PlayStation’s partnership in full swing, preorders being “heavily skewed” toward PS5 shouldn’t come as much of a surprise to anyone. The Verge’s report also suggested that the Xbox “reset,” led by new CEO Asha Sharma, might be about making Xbox easier to spin off or operate as a wholly owned subsidiary, as has been suggested by prior reports elsewhere. GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S only on November 19.
